attempts.note: The API is still live on 2026-11-13: the Django REST Framework root answers 200 with a router listing (resources under /api/v6/) and every resource answers 401 'Authentication credentials were not provided'. No schema is served: ?format=openapi and ?format=corejson 404 (JSON), /api/schema/, /api/docs/, /api/swagger/, /api/openapi.json and app.beyonic.com/api/swagger.json 404. OPTIONS metadata also requires a token.

Now 301-redirects to https://developers.onafriq.com/ (a Stoplight portal, workspace 'onafriq'). The Beyonic pages indexed there (/docs/collection-requests-api, /docs/payments-api, /docs/api-overview) return 404, as do /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt and /openapi.json; the Stoplight project API was not reachable anonymously. The legacy MFS Africa hub developer.mfsafrica.com does not resolve. web.archive.org was unreachable from this environment, so archived ReadMe-era copies could not be checked.

Vendor's own Slate source for the Beyonic API reference (last commit 2021-03-02). No OpenAPI/Postman file in the repo. Every include was read; it is the inventory: payments, collection requests, collections, contacts, webhooks, networks, banks, accounts, transactions, events, currencies, plus pagination, filtering, ordering, metadata, versioning, duplicate-request and error conventions.
Vendor SDK builds URLs from resource names at runtime; carries no spec and adds no endpoints beyond the docs.
no beyonic / onafriq / mfs africa entry.
no Beyonic/Onafriq public Postman workspace found by web search.
POST {apiUrl}/payments, /contacts, /collectionrequests (JSON, Authorization: Token <apiToken>, via Client.js). All three are in openapi.json.

notes: Beyonic was acquired by MFS Africa (now Onafriq). The API itself is NOT retired: on 2026-11-13 https://api.beyonic.com/api/ still serves its DRF router root (resources under /api/v6/) and every resource answers 401 without a token, but the public docs are gone (apidocs.beyonic.com redirects to the Onafriq Stoplight portal, where the Beyonic pages 404). The best surviving vendor evidence is the Slate source in github.com/beyonic/api-docs (2021), from which this spec was authored: 21 paths / 27 operations covering every documented resource (payments incl. bulk and bank payments, collection requests incl. recurring, collections incl. claiming, contacts, webhooks CRUD, accounts, transactions, events, networks, banks, currencies), DRF {count,next,previous,results} pagination, filters, ordering, Beyonic-Version and Duplicate-Check-Key headers; webhook and collection-verification payloads are component schemas. best-effort/partial-docs because the live router also exposes resources the 2021 docs never described (wallettransfer, reversals, paybill, validatebill, organizations, uploadkyc, senddocuments, collectionrequest-bank-account-ready, papitransactions, kibana_b2c/kibana_c2b); their methods and shapes are unknown, so they are not modelled. Decimal amounts are strings as in the doc samples; doc sample names and phone numbers were not copied as examples.
